key_insight: A trap-embedded CKD medication-review benchmark showed that current frontier LLMs can miss important nephrology-specific drug problems and sometimes hallucinate unsafe details.
clinical_relevance: For CKD patients with polypharmacy, LLM-assisted medication review may help workflow but should not be used without strong domain guardrails and human oversight.
method: 50 synthetic CKD cases across G3a-G3b, G4, and G5/G5D/transplant groups
8–12 medications per case with at least 2 embedded clinical traps
Five LLMs each generated 3 independent open-ended reviews per case and were scored against nephrologist-adjudicated gold standards
evidence_signal: Macro F1 ranged from 0.41 to 0.49, safety-critical omissions were 22%–48%, and hallucinations ranged from 0% to 54% across models.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is synthetic and not prospectively tested on real patients, deployment conclusions should be cautious until human-comparator validation is done.
paper_title: Frontier Large Language Models for Comprehensive Medication Review in CKD Patients with Polypharmacy: A Trap-Embedded Synthetic Benchmark
